text:
[RCLI.5.3] **A compile reports every error it finds, not the first.** Within one
stage of analysis a compiler must not stop at its first error; it reports each
one, as a separate diagnostic. It may stop before a later stage once an earlier
stage has failed, because the later stage's input is then not well-formed and
what it would report would be noise.

An author fixing a program should see the whole of what is wrong with it at the
point the compiler got to, not discover it one rebuild at a time.
